THROUGHLINE SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — CONFLICT-HEAVY AI WORKSHOP
Organization: Meridian Health Cooperative (fictional)
Date: June 20, 2026, 1:00 PM America/Chicago
Attendees: Dr. Sofia Patel (Chief Clinical Officer), Ben Ortiz (CIO), Dana Kim (Privacy), Marcus Lee (Program Manager), Alex Grant (Throughline user)

Alex: We are reviewing the clinical-documentation assistant initiative and what has changed since discovery.
Marcus: The initiative is in pilot and starts July 1.
Ben: That is not correct. We approved technical validation, not a clinical pilot. The earliest pilot would be August.
Sofia: I told the clinical leads we were targeting late July, assuming privacy clears it.
Dana: Privacy has not cleared it. We have not completed the data-protection assessment.
Marcus: The vendor said the environment is HIPAA ready.
Dana: Vendor readiness is not our approval. We still need the BAA amendment and retention terms.
Ben: The current system of record says the stage is solution proposed. Keep it there until validation is complete.
Alex: Who is the executive sponsor?
Sofia: I am.
Marcus: Ben has been acting as sponsor for the budget request.
Ben: I am the technical sponsor. Sofia owns the clinical outcome.
Alex: Then we should record separate executive and technical sponsorship rather than pick one.
Sofia: Agreed.
Dana: The use case may process psychotherapy notes.
Sofia: No, psychotherapy notes are excluded.
Marcus: The requirements document from May included them.
Dana: That document is outdated. The June 12 steering decision excluded them.
Alex: Please send the June 12 decision record.
Dana: I will send it today.
Ben: We need a limited dataset for validation by next Friday.
Marcus: Next Friday means June 26, right?
Ben: I meant July 3; I was looking at the wrong week.
Dana: July 3 is a holiday for much of the team. July 6 is more realistic.
Sofia: Let's not commit to a date until data engineering responds.
Alex: I will capture the date as unresolved and create a question, not a commitment.
Marcus: The vendor proposal is $240,000.
Ben: That includes optional services. The base proposal is $185,000.
Dana: Neither amount is approved.
Sofia: Our success metric is a 20 percent reduction in after-hours documentation.
Marcus: I have 30 percent in my notes.
Sofia: Twenty percent is the approved target. Thirty was the stretch goal.
Ben: We also require no measurable increase in coding errors.
Dana: And zero use of excluded note types.
Alex: The next formal gate is privacy and security validation, followed by a clinical-governance review.
All: Agreed.
Marcus: I can schedule the governance review for July 10.
Dana: Do not schedule it yet. We need the assessment first.
Alex: I will draft the proposed sequence, but no meeting will be scheduled without approval.
